newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 23.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Congress resumes the session today, focussing on the trade liberalisation bill and the 476.2 billion peso national budget. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- At least 27 F-16 planes and 15 other military cargo aircraft will land at Clark Airfield during the coming Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. The aircraft will be used in covert operations to secure the 18 leaders who will attend the APEC summit in November. (TODAY)
- The House of Representatives is expected to expedite approval of the remaining components of the Consolidated Tax Reform Package when it resumes its session today after a week-long recess. (TODAY)

- Only one of the five consortia which had earlier expressed interest in bidding for the $400 million Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 3 project submitted an offer to the Department of Transportation and Communications on Friday. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The government will begin to cut down an estimated 600 billion pesos worth of internal debt accumulated through some 20 years of financial misrule by an initial 24.7 billion pesos in 1997, according to the Department of Finance. The amount represents treasury bills that it will cut from a programmed but undisclosed amount of debt issues planned for next year. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)
